## Personality

Bold, restless and always the first to volunteer; she climbs the stairs two at a time for fun.

## Lore

Moira is twenty-one and a guard of the Cliff Watch, the band that keeps the cliff stairs of Goa Harbour and the paths that come down to them from the forest. She is bold, restless and always the first to volunteer, and she climbs the stairs two at a time for fun, from the Inlet Quay to the clifftop, and then goes back down to do it again. The other guards have stopped trying to keep up with her. Ruan, her captain, has stopped trying to make her walk.

### Why she joined

Moira grew up in a cliff house above the Inlet Quay and spent her childhood listening to the hunters at the Gap Inn talk about the things they had seen on the wild coast. She joined the Cliff Watch at seventeen, four years ago, for one reason only: she wanted to see a monster up close. In those days the watch still spent most nights walking the stairs with lanterns and seeing nothing at all, and for her first year she was bitterly disappointed.

Then, three winters ago, a creature came up the cliff face itself, not down the forest paths, and reached the high landing before anyone could stop it. Moira was on watch. She was the one who ran to the head of the Long Stair and rang the iron bar, and she was close enough afterward to see Torva and two of her hunters drive the thing back over the edge, and to see what it had done to Torva's jaw. She had wanted to see a monster up close. Since then she has seen far more of them than she wanted, and she has never once said so out loud.

### Torva and the stairs

Moira admires Torva more than anyone in Goa Harbour, and says so to anyone who will listen. Torva counts her a friend, which Moira still finds hard to believe. Moira would much rather be out on the wild coast with Torva's hunters than climbing the stairs every night, and she has asked Torva, more than once, to take her. Each time Torva tells her that the stairs need her more. Moira thinks Torva is being kind. Ruan knows Torva is telling the truth, and he keeps Moira on the watch and says nothing about it.

She works hard for Ruan, even when she is sulking about the hunters. She volunteers for the high landings, the darkest stretches of the cliff and the late watches nobody else wants, because that is where the climbers come. She has helped carry Ruan's demands for more lanterns to Gunna's workshop, and she has made friends with Tarran, the apprentice, because he is the only person who has promised her a lantern sooner. She knows Kestra from the bridges, and they race each other up the stairs some evenings. Kestra usually wins, and Moira usually claims she let her.

### What she wants and fears

Moira wants to go out with the hunters, just once, into the forest and back. She wants to prove she is as good as any of them. What she fears she keeps to herself: that one of these nights she will be the one at the bar again, and that this time there will be nobody like Torva near enough to come.

She has noticed that the climbers are coming more often, always on the darkest nights, and that they seem to be getting better at finding the parts of the cliff the lanterns do not reach. She has said this to Ruan. He nodded and wrote it down, and his face told her he already knew.

### Hooks

A quest might stand a night watch on the high landings with Moira, persuade Torva to let her go out with the hunters for a single day, or race her up the Long Stair for a wager she has no intention of losing.
